slides.headline: He found the genetic switch behind the most common prostate cancer mutation. It just won him medicine's Harrington Prize.
Dr. Arul M. Chinnaiyan won the 2026 International Harrington Prize for Innovation in Medicine, shared with Dr. Charles Sawyers
slides.body: A second-generation Indian-American and Howard Hughes Medical Institute Investigator at the University of Michigan, Chinnaiyan discovered the TMPRSS2-ERG gene fusion - the most common genetic alteration found in prostate cancer.

slides.headline: His work helped identify which prostate cancer mutations respond to specific drugs, not just which patients have cancer.
slides.body: His research into mutations that respond to PARP inhibitors like olaparib turned a one-size-fits-all disease into one doctors could increasingly treat based on a patient's specific genetics - precision medicine instead of guesswork.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs its scientists finding the genetic mechanisms that let medicine stop guessing.
slides.body: Chinnaiyan's discovery didn't just explain prostate cancer - it became the first University of Michigan work to win this particular prize, built on exactly the kind of mechanism-first science precision medicine depends on.
